endpoints.summary: Patient requests a refill on one of their own prescriptions. Flips refillStatus to PENDING, stamps refillRequestedAt, overwrites refillNotes with the supplied notes (or null), and fires a REFILL_REQUEST notification to the prescribing physician. Responds with only two fields — NOT the full prescription.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) at L20 (JWT Bearer -> req.user {id, userType, ...}). No auditLog, no aiUsageCheck. In-handler gate: prescription.visit.patientUserId must === req.user.id (patient-only; the prescribing physician gets 403 here). No userType check — any user who is the visit's patient passes, regardless of userType claim.
endpoints.responseShape: { "refillStatus": "PENDING", "refillRequestedAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:33.123Z" }  // exactly 2 keys. refillStatus is always the literal string "PENDING" (it is what was just written). refillRequestedAt is a DateTime serialized by JSON as an ISO-8601 string with milliseconds and trailing Z. No id, no medications, no message key.
requestBody: notes?: string (optional; any other body keys are ignored). Body may be entirely empty ({}) — that is what both client callers send (PrescriptionPanel.jsx L228, PrescriptionsPage.jsx L254).
dbWrites: prescriptions: UPDATE refillRequestedAt=now(), refillStatus='PENDING', refillNotes=notes||null (no transaction)
notifications: INSERT (userId=physician.userId, type='REFILL_REQUEST') — inside try/catch, best-effort
ai/email/push: no DB write; push tokens read by pushService
crossModelReads: User (patient displayName for the notification message)
PhysicianProfile (by prescription.physicianId, select userId)
Notification (created via notificationService)
externalDeps: pushService.send — always attempted by createNotification, best-effort
sideEffects: Notification row for the physician: type 'REFILL_REQUEST', title 'Prescription Refill Request', message `${patient.displayName || 'A patient'} requested a prescription refill.`, data { prescriptionId: id }
Web push attempt to the physician (title/body = the notification title/message)
No email (sendEmail: false)
No cache invalidation — GET /api/prescriptions is cached 15s per-user and GET /summary 30s, so the requesting patient's own list can still show the pre-refill state for up to 15s
errorCases: 404 {"error":"Prescription not found"} when no Prescription row with that id (note: the model has deletedAt but findUnique does NOT filter it, so soft-deleted prescriptions are still refillable)
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when prescription.visit.patientUserId !== req.user.id

400 {"error":"Can only request refill on sent/dispensed prescriptions"} when status is not one of SENT, DISPENSED, CONFIRMED (note: message says sent/dispensed but CONFIRMED is also allowed; DRAFT and SIGNED are rejected)
400 {"error":"Refill request already pending"} when prescription.refillStatus === 'PENDING'
500 {"error":"Failed to request refill"} on any thrown error
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global /api limiter (100 req/min/IP)
quirks: Response is a 2-key projection, not the prescription. A port that returns the updated row breaks nothing visibly today (clients ignore the body and refetch) but violates byte-identity.

refillNotes is ALWAYS overwritten: `refillNotes: notes || null`. Re-requesting after an APPROVED/DENIED decision silently WIPES the physician's previous refillNotes to null. An empty-string notes also writes null.
Status gate allows CONFIRMED even though the error message only mentions sent/dispensed. Order of the allowed list in code is ['SENT','DISPENSED','CONFIRMED'].

refillStatus is a plain String column (not an enum) in Prisma — values are the bare strings 'PENDING'/'APPROVED'/'DENIED', and NULL for never-requested. A .NET port must NOT model it as a non-nullable enum.
Only refillStatus === 'PENDING' blocks; APPROVED or DENIED lets the patient immediately re-request, resetting to PENDING.
No status transition guard beyond the above — a prescription can be refill-requested repeatedly after each decision.
The notification block is wrapped in try/catch; if PhysicianProfile lookup returns null NO notification is created and the request still returns 200.

The global XSS sanitizer (index.js L57-L81) mutates req.body BEFORE the handler: `notes` has HTML tags/on*= handlers stripped, `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` prefixes removed, and every `url(` rewritten to `url\(`. The stored refillNotes is the sanitized string, not the raw client string. A .NET port must reproduce this or stored values differ.
No deletedAt filter anywhere in this file.
Route ordering: PUT /:id (L242) does not shadow these two-segment routes; POST / (L99) does not shadow /check-interactions or /transcribe-rx. No shadowing affects any of the 7 endpoints.

endpoints.summary: Prescribing physician approves or denies a pending refill. Writes refillStatus = the action string and conditionally updates refillNotes, then emails+notifies the patient. Returns a 2-key projection.
endpoints.auth: authCheck (router-level). No auditLog, no aiUsageCheck. In-handler gate: PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND prescription.physicianId === physician.id. Patients always get 403.
endpoints.responseShape: { "refillStatus": "APPROVED", "refillNotes": "Refill ok for 30 days" }  // exactly 2 keys. refillStatus is the literal action string sent by the caller ('APPROVED' or 'DENIED'). refillNotes is a nullable string — null when neither the request nor the prior row had notes. No id, no message, no timestamps.
requestBody: action: string, REQUIRED, must be exactly 'APPROVED' or 'DENIED' (case-sensitive, uppercase)
dbWrites: prescriptions: UPDATE refillStatus=action, refillNotes=(notes || existing refillNotes) (no transaction)
notifications: INSERT for the patient — best-effort inside try/catch
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (ownership check by userId)
Notification (via notificationService)
User (read inside createNotification for the email address)
sideEffects: Notification for prescription.visit.patientUserId: type 'REFILL_RESPONSE', title `Refill Approved` or `Refill Denied`, message `Your prescription refill request has been approved.` / `...denied.` with `` ` Note: ${notes}` `` appended only when notes is truthy

EMAIL sent to the patient (sendEmail: true): subject = the title, html = `

${title}

${message}

`, text = `${title}\n\n${message}`
Web push attempt
No cache invalidation of the 15s/30s GET caches
errorCases: 400 {"error":"Action must be APPROVED or DENIED"} when action is not exactly 'APPROVED' or 'DENIED' — this check runs FIRST, before the prescription is even loaded, so a bad action on a nonexistent id returns 400, not 404
404 {"error":"Prescription not found"}
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when the caller has no PhysicianProfile or is not the prescriber
400 {"error":"No pending refill request"} when prescription.refillStatus !== 'PENDING' (including null)
500 {"error":"Failed to respond to refill"}
401 from authCheck; 429 from the global limiter
quirks: Validation order matters for byte-identity: action validation precedes the 404/403 checks.
`action` is written verbatim into the refillStatus String column — a port must store the raw uppercase string, not an enum ordinal.

refillNotes uses `notes || prescription.refillNotes` — an empty string or omitted notes PRESERVES the previous value (opposite of refill-request, which nulls it). The two endpoints treat refillNotes inconsistently.
The notification title uses a ternary on APPROVED, so DENIED (and only DENIED, since other values are rejected) yields 'Refill Denied'.
The message embeds `action.toLowerCase()` -> 'approved'/'denied'.
Note suffix is `' Note: ' + notes` — a single leading space after the period, no comma. Byte-exact for the email/notification body.
refillRequestedAt is NOT cleared on response — it keeps the original request timestamp.
This endpoint sends a real email; the refill-request endpoint deliberately does not (sendEmail:false there, true here).
No transaction: if the Notification insert fails the prescription update still stands (caught and logged).
Global XSS sanitizer rewrites `notes` before it is stored and before it is interpolated into the email HTML.

endpoints.summary: Patient marks one medication inside the prescription's medications JSON array as stopped by adding stoppedAt + stoppedByPatient to that element. Returns a message and the FULL in-memory medications array (not the DB row).
endpoints.auth: authCheck (router-level). No auditLog, no aiUsageCheck, no status gate. In-handler gate: prescription.visit.patientUserId === req.user.id (patient-only; the prescribing physician gets 403).
endpoints.responseShape: { "message": "Stopped Amoxicillin", "medications": [ { "drugName": "Amoxicillin", "dosage": "500mg", "frequency": "Three times daily", "duration": "7 days", "instructions": "", "stoppedAt": "2026-09-03T10:22:33.123Z", "stoppedByPatient": true }, { ...untouched original elements, passed through verbatim... } ] }  // 2 keys. `medications` is the whole array, not just the changed element. Element keys are whatever the stored JSON had (typically drugName/dosage/frequency/duration/instructions as written by POST / or by the AI extractors) PLUS the two stop flags on the targeted index only. stoppedAt is a STRING (new Date().toISOString()), not a Date — it is generated with .toISOString() in the handler, so it is a string both in the response and in the persisted JSON column. The array is [] (empty array, never null) when the stored medications value was not an array.
requestBody: medicationIndex: REQUIRED (rejected only when undefined or null). Declared as a number; no typeof check is performed.
dbWrites: prescriptions: UPDATE medications = <the whole rebuilt array> (whole-column JSON overwrite, no transaction)
sideEffects: None — no notification, no email, no push, no audit row.

No reminder cleanup: the DAILY medication Reminder rows auto-created by PUT /:id/send are NOT cancelled or deleted when a medication is stopped. The patient keeps receiving reminders for a stopped drug.
No cache invalidation.
errorCases: 400 {"error":"medicationIndex is required"} ONLY when medicationIndex === undefined || === null (0 passes correctly; '' , false and NaN all pass this check)
404 {"error":"Prescription not found"}
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when the caller is not the visit's patient
400 {"error":"Invalid medication index"} when medicationIndex < 0 or >= meds.length — meds is [] when the stored medications JSON is not an array, so every index is then invalid
500 {"error":"Failed to stop medication"}
401 from authCheck; 429 from the global limiter
quirks: Returns the in-memory `meds` array, NOT the prisma update result. A port must echo the array it just built, and must include untouched elements verbatim (all original keys, in original key order).

stoppedAt is a string-formatted ISO-8601 date (new Date().toISOString()), not a Date/DateTime. In SQL Server this must stay a string inside the JSON column — do not round-trip it through DateTime formatting that drops milliseconds or the Z.
stoppedByPatient is the literal boolean true.

The element is REPLACED with a spread copy: `{...meds[i], stoppedAt, stoppedByPatient}`. Original key order is preserved and the two new keys are appended last. Byte-identical JSON requires the same key ordering.

NaN index bypass: a non-numeric medicationIndex (e.g. "abc") passes both bounds checks (NaN comparisons are false), so `meds["abc"] = {...undefined, stoppedAt, stoppedByPatient}` sets a NON-INDEX property on the array. JSON.stringify drops it, so the DB write is a no-op, and the response is 200 with message "Stopped undefined" and an unchanged medications array. A faithful port must reproduce this 200 + "Stopped undefined" behavior, not 400.
String indices work by numeric coercion: medicationIndex "1" passes the bounds checks and meds["1"] resolves the array element.
message is a template literal: `Stopped ${meds[medicationIndex].drugName}` — if the element has no drugName the message reads "Stopped undefined" (still 200).
No status gate at all: a patient can stop a medication on a DRAFT or SIGNED (never-sent) prescription, as long as it is on their visit.
No deletedAt filter — soft-deleted prescriptions are still mutable here.
Stopped medications are excluded from cross-prescription drug interaction checks (check-interactions filters on !m.stoppedAt), so this write silently changes that endpoint's result.
Whole-array overwrite means concurrent stop/resume calls last-write-wins with no optimistic concurrency.

endpoints.summary: Patient un-stops a medication by destructuring stoppedAt and stoppedByPatient off the element and writing the cleaned array back. Mirror of stop-medication but WITHOUT the required-field check.
endpoints.auth: authCheck (router-level). No auditLog, no aiUsageCheck, no status gate. In-handler gate: prescription.visit.patientUserId === req.user.id.
endpoints.responseShape: { "message": "Resumed Amoxicillin", "medications": [ { "drugName": "Amoxicillin", "dosage": "500mg", "frequency": "Three times daily", "duration": "7 days", "instructions": "" }, { ...other elements verbatim... } ] }  // 2 keys. The targeted element has stoppedAt and stoppedByPatient REMOVED (keys absent, not null); all other keys survive with their original relative order. medications is [] (empty array, never null) when the stored value was not an array.
requestBody: medicationIndex: number — NOT validated for presence (unlike stop-medication). Only bounds-checked.
dbWrites: prescriptions: UPDATE medications = <the whole rebuilt array> (no transaction)
sideEffects: None — no notification, email, push, audit, or reminder re-creation. Resuming does NOT restore the medication Reminder rows (they were never deleted by stop, so they simply continued).
No cache invalidation.
errorCases: 404 {"error":"Prescription not found"}
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"}
400 {"error":"Invalid medication index"} when medicationIndex < 0 or >= meds.length
500 {"error":"Failed to resume medication"} — notably this is what a MISSING medicationIndex produces (see quirks), not a 400
401 from authCheck; 429 from the global limiter
quirks: MISSING medicationIndex yields 500, not 400. There is no `is required` check: undefined passes both bounds comparisons (undefined < 0 and undefined >= n are both false), then `const { stoppedAt, stoppedByPatient, ...cleanMed } = meds[undefined]` destructures undefined and throws a TypeError, caught as 500 {"error":"Failed to resume medication"}. This asymmetry with stop-medication (which returns 400) must be preserved.

null medicationIndex behaves differently again: `null < 0` is false and `null >= n` is false for n>0, so it also reaches the destructure of meds[null] -> undefined -> 500. But when meds is [] , `null >= 0` is TRUE, so it returns 400 'Invalid medication index'.
NaN/non-numeric index ("abc") passes bounds, meds["abc"] is undefined, destructuring undefined throws -> 500 (whereas stop-medication returns 200 for the same input).

Key REMOVAL, not nulling: the response element must omit stoppedAt/stoppedByPatient entirely. A port that sets them to null produces a different JSON body and the client's `med.stoppedAt` truthiness check for the Stop/Resume button still works but the byte contract is broken.
Rest-spread reorders nothing for the surviving keys, but the cleaned element is a NEW object — original insertion order of the remaining keys is preserved.

message is `Resumed ${meds[medicationIndex].drugName}` computed AFTER the element was replaced by cleanMed; if the original element only had stoppedAt/stoppedByPatient (no drugName) the message is "Resumed undefined" with a 200.
Resuming an element that was never stopped is a legal no-op returning 200 with the array unchanged.
No status gate, no deletedAt filter, whole-array last-write-wins, same as stop-medication.

endpoints.summary: Aggregates the caller-supplied drug names with every active drug it can discover for the patient (subprofile CurrentMedication rows, all non-stopped medications across all their prescriptions from any physician, and all family subprofiles' current meds), dedupes them, then runs the two-stage OpenFDA + LLM checker and logs an InteractionAlert row. Returns interactions + drugsChecked + a message.
endpoints.auth: authCheck ONLY (router-level). NO aiUsageCheck (this AI endpoint is unmetered, unlike transcribe-rx), NO auditLog, NO physician/patient gate, NO ownership check on subprofileId or visitId. Any authenticated user may pass any visitId or subprofileId.
endpoints.responseShape:
Two distinct 200 shapes.

(A) Early return when fewer than 2 distinct drugs resolve (L806):
{ "interactions": [], "drugsChecked": ["Metformin"], "message": "Only 1 active medication found — no interactions to check" }
  - interactions is ALWAYS an empty array here (never null)
  - drugsChecked is the deduped array, possibly [] (empty array, never null)
  - message is exactly "No active medications found" when drugsChecked.length === 0, otherwise exactly "Only 1 active medication found — no interactions to check" (note the EM DASH U+2014 surrounded by single spaces)

(B) Normal AI path (L863):
{
  "interactions": [
    {
      "drug1": "Amoxicillin",
      "drug2": "ALLERGY: Penicillin",
      "severity": "HIGH",
      "description": "Patient has a documented allergy to Penicillin. Amoxicillin may cause an allergic reaction.",
      "recommendation": "DO NOT prescribe. Consider alternatives.",
      "alternatives": []
    },
    {
      "drug1": "Warfarin",
      "drug2": "Ibuprofen",
      "severity": "MODERATE",
      "description": "...",
      "recommendation": "...",
      "alternatives": ["Acetaminophen"]
    }
  ],
  "drugsChecked": ["Warfarin", "Ibuprofen", "Amoxicillin"],
  "message": "2 interaction(s) found"
}
  - interactions = [...deterministic string-match allergy warnings FIRST, ...LLM/FDA-derived entries SECOND]
  - the LLM-derived entries are RAW JSON.parse output of model text: the six keys above are only what the prompt asks for and are NOT enforced by code. Missing/extra keys are passed through untouched.
  - alternatives is an array (may be empty); it is never normalized.
  - message is exactly `${n} interaction(s) found` when n > 0, else exactly "No known interactions detected"
  - drugsChecked is the same deduped array that was sent to the checker, in insertion order: caller-supplied medications first, then discovered drugs
requestBody: medications?: array (defaults to [] via destructuring default; also treated as [] if not an array). The client sends an array of plain DRUG NAME STRINGS (PrescriptionPanel L158/L218, DrugScreeningsPage L82/L109, PatientProfilePage L160). PrescriptionsPage L266 sends an entirely empty body {}.
subprofileId?: string — used unvalidated to pull CurrentMedication rows and (with allergies/conditions) build AI context
visitId?: string — used unvalidated to resolve visit.patientUserId
dbWrites: interaction_alerts: INSERT { physicianId: physician?.id || null, patientUserId: !physician ? req.user.id : null, drugs: allDrugs (JSON), interactions: result.interactions (JSON), alertCount: result.interactions.length } — wrapped in try/catch, failure is logged and swallowed
ai_audit_logs: INSERT via aiGateway.logAudit for the drug_check chat call and for the checkDrugs summary (provider recorded as 'fda_label+llm' or 'llm_only')
crossModelReads: CurrentMedication (findMany where subprofileId + isActive, select drugName)
Visit (findUnique by visitId, select patientUserId)
Prescription (findMany where visit.patientUserId and status in SIGNED/CONFIRMED/SENT/DISPENSED, select medications)
FamilySubprofile (findMany where patientProfile.userId = patientUserId, select id; and findFirst for the allergy/condition context subprofile)
Allergy (findMany where subprofileId + isActive, select allergen)
ChronicCondition (findMany where subprofileId + isActive, select name)
PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId, only to decide which column of the InteractionAlert row to fill)
InteractionAlert (create)
AiAuditLog (create, inside aiGateway)
externalDeps: OpenFDA https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json — one HTTP GET per unordered drug PAIR, sequential
OpenFDA https://api.fda.gov/drug/event.json — one HTTP GET per pair, sequential
aiGateway.chat -> OpenAI/Gemini/MicroMind chain (agent 'drug_check' routes to gemini-2.0-flash first), temperature 0.1, maxTokens 2000, useCache:false
sideEffects: InteractionAlert history row (surfaced by GET /interaction-history)
AiAuditLog rows that count toward the monthly AI quota of OTHER endpoints (this endpoint itself is unmetered but its logAudit rows are what aiUsageCheck counts elsewhere)
Outbound calls to api.fda.gov — O(n^2) requests in the number of drugs, twice (labels + events), no caching, no parallelism, no timeout
No notification, no email
errorCases: 500 {"error":"Failed to check interactions"} on any throw (including an object-typed entry in `medications` reaching drug.toLowerCase() when the patient has allergies, and any unhandled prisma error)
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
NOTE: there is NO 400 and NO 403 on this route at all — no input validation, no role check, no ownership check
quirks: The "Only 1 active medication found — no interactions to check" message contains an EM DASH (—, U+2014) with a space on each side. Byte-identical output requires the exact character.
"${n} interaction(s) found" — literal parenthesised (s), never pluralized differently.

IDOR: visitId and subprofileId are never authorization-checked. Any authenticated user can pass another patient's visitId and receive that patient's full active drug list back in `drugsChecked`. A faithful port reproduces this; flag it to the team rather than silently fixing it, because the response contract depends on it.

Caller identity fallback: when visitId is absent and req.user.userType !== 'PHYSICIAN', patientUserId defaults to req.user.id — so a physician calling with no visitId gets NO auto-discovery (only the drugs they typed), while a patient gets full auto-discovery. Same request body, different result by userType.
The all-family-subprofiles sweep runs ONLY when subprofileId is falsy. Passing subprofileId narrows discovery to that one subprofile.

Allergy/condition context uses `subprofileId || (findFirst FamilySubprofile for patientUserId)` with NO orderBy — the chosen subprofile is DB-order-arbitrary, so a patient's allergies may actually be a random family member's. Wrapped in a bare `catch { }` that silently continues with empty allergies.

Deduplication is `[...new Set([...inputMeds, ...existingDrugs].filter(Boolean))]` — CASE SENSITIVE. "Aspirin" and "aspirin" are two distinct drugs in drugsChecked and generate an extra FDA pair lookup.

Ordering of drugsChecked is insertion order: caller medications first, then subprofile CurrentMedication, then prescription medications (in prescription then array order), then family subprofile meds. A port using a HashSet loses this order and changes the JSON.
Stopped medications are skipped via `.filter(m => !m.stoppedAt)`; the fallback `.map(m => m.drugName || m)` means a medications array of bare strings is also supported.
Prescription discovery includes SIGNED (never sent) prescriptions, and does NOT filter deletedAt.

interactions entries are unvalidated LLM JSON. The client (DrugScreeningsPage L91-L101) reads only drug1/drug2/severity/description/recommendation and maps severity HIGH->SEVERE, MODERATE->MODERATE, LOW->MILD, falling through to the raw value for anything else — so severity is contractually one of the three uppercase strings but not enforced.

Two different fallback shapes exist inside checkDrugs when the LLM output is unparseable or the LLM call throws: entries become { drug1, drug2, severity, description, recommendation: 'Review patient history and monitor closely.', alternatives: [] } with severity derived as 'MODERATE' for fda_label source, else eventCount > 100 -> 'HIGH', > 20 -> 'MODERATE', else 'LOW', and description falling back to `FDA reports ${eventCount || '?'} adverse events. Reactions: ${reactions.join(', ')}`.

Allergy string-match warnings are PREPENDED (allergyWarnings first, then enrichedInteractions) and use bidirectional substring matching, so a patient allergic to "Pen" flags every drug containing "pen".
This endpoint bypasses aiUsageCheck entirely — a FREE-tier user has unlimited drug checks here while transcribe-rx is capped. Do not "fix" this during the port without a decision.
useCache:false on the reasoning chat means every call hits the model; results are never deduped.
The handler ignores checkDrugs' own drugsChecked and re-emits its local allDrugs (same reference, so identical output).
The global XSS sanitizer rewrites every string in medications before use (e.g. a drug name containing `url(` becomes `url\(`), which then propagates into drugsChecked and the FDA query strings.

endpoints.summary: Physician-only. Sends the SOAP Plan free text to the LLM and returns a normalized array of medication objects. Always 200 with a medications array once the physician gate passes — parse failures are swallowed and return an empty array with no error key.
endpoints.auth: authCheck (router-level). NO aiUsageCheck (unmetered AI call). NO auditLog. In-handler gate: a PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id, else 403.
endpoints.responseShape: { "medications": [ { "drugName": "Amoxicillin", "dosage": "500mg", "frequency": "Three times daily", "duration": "7 days", "instructions": "" } ] }  // exactly 1 key. Every element has exactly these 5 keys in exactly this order, every value a trimmed STRING (never null, never undefined — missing fields become ""). medications is [] (empty array, never null) when the AI returned nothing, returned non-array JSON, threw a parse error, or produced text with no [...] block. There is NO parseError key on this endpoint (unlike transcribe-rx) and NO count/message key.
requestBody: planText: string, REQUIRED. Must be truthy and planText.trim().length >= 5.
dbWrites: No other writes — this endpoint creates no Prescription
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId — existence gate only)
AiAuditLog (created inside aiGateway)
externalDeps: aiGateway.chat (lazily required) with temperature 0.1, maxTokens 1000, useCache:false, metadata { agent: 'specialty_extract', userId }
Provider chain: 'specialty_extract' is NOT in AGENT_MODEL_DEFAULTS, so it uses AI_PRIMARY_PROVIDER (default 'openai', gpt-4o) then AI_FALLBACK_PROVIDER (default 'gemini') then 'micromind'
sideEffects: AiAuditLog row(s) — these count toward the caller's monthly AI quota enforced by aiUsageCheck on OTHER endpoints
logger.info with the extracted count
No DB writes to prescriptions, no notification, no email
errorCases: 400 {"error":"Plan text is required"} when planText is falsy OR planText.trim().length < 5
403 {"error":"Only physicians can extract prescriptions"} when no PhysicianProfile for req.user.id

500 {"error":"Failed to extract medications"} on any throw — including a non-string planText (planText.trim is not a function), and including aiGateway throwing 'AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: ...' or 'Prompt too long (N chars, max 50000)'
401 from authCheck; 429 from the global limiter
413 from express.json({limit:'10mb'}) for oversized bodies (handled by the global error handler)
quirks: A non-string planText (number, object, array) reaches `.trim()` and throws -> 500 {"error":"Failed to extract medications"}, NOT 400. Only null/undefined/'' /0/false take the 400 path.

AI parse failures are INVISIBLE to the client: the catch only logs, then the handler returns 200 { medications: [] }. The client (PrescriptionPanel L277) can only distinguish this from 'AI found nothing' by the empty array, and shows 'No medications found in the Plan text'. A port must NOT add an error field.

Extraction uses a GREEDY regex `/\[[\s\S]*\]/` on the raw model text — it matches from the FIRST '[' to the LAST ']' in the whole response. Prose containing brackets before or after the JSON array will corrupt the match and produce [] via the swallowed parse error. Reproduce the greedy regex, not a JSON-aware parser, or outputs diverge.
When the regex does NOT match at all, `medications` stays [] and NO catch runs — silent empty result.
When JSON.parse succeeds but yields a non-array (e.g. a single object), medications is reset to [] .
Filter is `m => m && m.drugName` — elements without a truthy drugName are DROPPED silently, so the returned array can be shorter than what the model produced and indices do not correspond.

Normalization forces String(...) then .trim() on all five fields, so a numeric dosage 500 from the model becomes the string "500". null/undefined become "" (because `String(m.x || '')`). Note the `|| ''` means a literal 0 or false also becomes "".
Key order in each element is fixed by the object literal: drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions. Byte-identical JSON depends on this order.
There is NO markdown code-fence stripping here (unlike transcribe-rx, which does .replace(/```json/) first) — extract-from-plan relies solely on the bracket regex, which happens to survive fences.
Unmetered: no aiUsageCheck, so a FREE-tier physician can call this without limit even though the parallel transcribe-rx endpoint is capped.

The global XSS sanitizer mutates planText before the LLM sees it: HTML tags, on*= handlers, `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` prefixes are stripped and every `url(` becomes `url\(`. A port that skips the sanitizer sends a different prompt and can get different medications back.
useCache:false — identical planText always re-hits the model (contrast with transcribe-rx's parse call, which caches).

endpoints.nodeLines: L960-L1069 (multer config L960-L969, aiUsageCheck import L970, route L972-L1069)
endpoints.summary: Physician-only voice dictation. Multipart audio -> Whisper transcript -> second LLM call that parses the transcript into structured medications. Returns transcript + medications, with a DIFFERENT response shape when the medication parse fails.
endpoints.auth: authCheck (router-level) -> rxUpload.single('audio') (multer, memory storage, 25MB, audio/* only) -> aiUsageCheck('scribe') -> handler. In-handler gate: PhysicianProfile must exist for req.user.id. NOTE the middleware order: the file is fully uploaded and buffered BEFORE the quota check, and the quota check runs BEFORE the physician check.
endpoints.responseShape:
Two distinct 200 shapes.

(A) Success (L1063):
{ "transcript": "Amoxicillin 500 milligrams three times a day for seven days", "medications": [ { "drugName": "Amoxicillin", "dosage": "500mg", "frequency": "Three times daily", "duration": "7 days", "instructions": "" } ], "transcribeDuration": 12.34 }

403 {"error":"Only physicians can dictate prescriptions"} when no PhysicianProfile for req.user.id
400 {"error":"Could not transcribe audio. Please try again."} when the transcript is empty or trim().length < 3 — charged for the Whisper call anyway

429 {"error":"Monthly AI limit reached", "message":"You've used 50/50 AI calls this month. Upgrade to Pro for more.", "upgradeRequired": true, "currentTier":"FREE", "usage": { "used": 50, "limit": 50, "totalTokens": 12345, "totalCost": 0.42, "resetsAt": "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z" }} from aiUsageCheck
401 {"error":"Authentication required"} or {"error":"User not found"} from aiUsageCheck (distinct bodies from authCheck's)

500 {"error": <RAW error.message>} — this handler returns error.message, e.g. {"error":"Transcription requires OPENAI_API_KEY (Whisper API)"} or {"error":"AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: ..."}, falling back to {"error":"Failed to transcribe prescription"} only when message is empty

500 {"error":"Only audio files are allowed"} from the GLOBAL error handler (index.js L311) when fileFilter rejects a non-audio mimetype — multer's cb(new Error(...)) has no .status, so err.status||500 yields 500, NOT 400
500 {"error":"File too large"} from the global error handler when the 25MB limit is exceeded (MulterError has .code but no .status)
In NODE_ENV=development the global error handler ALSO adds a "stack" key to those two bodies
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the global limiter
quirks: Two different success shapes: transcribeDuration is present on the happy path and ABSENT on the parseError path, and parseError is present only on the failure path. A port must not emit all four keys with nulls.

Middleware order is load-bearing: multer parses and buffers up to 25MB BEFORE aiUsageCheck runs, so an over-quota user still pays the upload; and aiUsageCheck runs BEFORE the physician check, so a PATIENT calling this gets 403 {"error":"Feature not available on your plan", ...upgradeRequired} — NOT 403 {"error":"Only physicians can dictate prescriptions"}. That second message is only reachable by a non-patient userType with no PhysicianProfile.
aiUsageCheck FAILS OPEN: any thrown error inside it (DB down, etc.) calls next() and the request proceeds unmetered.
This is the ONLY one of the seven endpoints with a quota check. check-interactions and extract-from-plan make AI calls with no metering.
500 bodies here leak the raw exception message (error.message), unlike every other handler in this file which uses a fixed string. A port must forward the underlying message.

language defaults to 'en', which DISABLES Whisper's auto-detection (aiGateway only sets whisperOptions.language when language is truthy) — so Arabic dictation is transcribed as English. The default is applied in the route, not the gateway.

The parse chat uses useCache:true (the default) with the cache key sha256(system + transcript) — two identical transcripts return the cached medications without a second model call, and the cached branch logs tokensUsed 0 / costUsd 0 so it does NOT count toward the monthly quota (aiUsageCheck filters cached:false).

metadata.agent is 'scribe' for the parse chat, which matches AGENT_MODEL_DEFAULTS.scribe = { provider:'openai', model:'whisper-1' }. Only the PROVIDER is used to reorder the chain — agentConfig.model is never passed to the provider fn — so the chat still runs on OPENAI_MODEL/gpt-4o, not whisper-1. Looks like a bug but is behaviorally inert; a port must not 'fix' it into actually selecting whisper-1.

Markdown fence stripping here is `.replace(/```json\n?/g,'').replace(/```\n?/g,'').trim()` then JSON.parse of the WHOLE cleaned string — different from extract-from-plan, which uses a greedy [...] regex instead. The two endpoints fail on different malformed outputs; both must be ported literally.
JSON.parse succeeding with a non-array yields medications = [] and NO parseError (falls through to shape A, including transcribeDuration).
Elements are filtered by `m && m.drugName` and normalized with String(x || '').trim() into exactly 5 keys in fixed order — same normalization as extract-from-plan.
transcript with trim().length < 3 returns 400 AFTER Whisper was billed and audited.

fileFilter rejects with an Error rather than cb(null,false), so a wrong mimetype surfaces as 500 'Only audio files are allowed'; but if it somehow yields no file, the handler's own 400 'No audio file provided' applies. Both paths exist.

The global XSS sanitizer does NOT touch this request's fields: it runs before multer populates req.body, so `language` reaches the handler unsanitized (contrast with every JSON-body endpoint in this file).
transcribeDuration is a float in SECONDS from Whisper's verbose_json, defaulted to 0 — not milliseconds, not a formatted string.
